This Custom Island Tiny House Offers All the Comforts of a Full-Size Home and Storage Galore
25 photos
Photo: Tiny House Expedition/YouTube screenshot
People decide to live in tiny houses for different reasons. For some, it’s their only chance at homeownership, while others want to simplify their lives, minimize their environmental footprint, or enjoy the freedom of living anywhere they want. For Steph and Katie, tiny living offered a great way to make the most of their remote property on the Southern Gulf Islands of British Columbia.
Steph and Katie have an absolutely dreamy tiny house on wheels parked among the trees on their 1.5-acre property, and for them, it was just the perfect solution to fully enjoy island life. Their tiny home was built by Summit Tiny Homes, a leading luxury tiny house builder in Canada, and is a custom unit based on the company’s Modern Bohemian model.
Perched on a sloped hill, the home feels truly connected to its surroundings. It features a modern rustic exterior clad in a combination of black metal siding and natural wood slats, which allows it to blend in with the natural environment. Working closely with the builder, Steph and Katie got to fully customize their home to perfectly meet their needs and tastes. From layout details to finishes and decor, everything has been carefully curated to create a space that reflects their personalities.
Next to it, Steph and Katie installed a separate office pod that offers 100 square feet of space and serves as both a workspace for the two of them and as guest accommodation. It was also built by Summit Tiny Homes and represents a useful addition that extends the functionality of the property.
Photo: Tiny House Expedition/YouTube screenshot Offering a harmonious mix of charm, comfort, and luxury, their custom Modern Bohemian tiny house is built on a triple-axle trailer and measures 37.5 feet (11.4 meters) long, 8.5 feet (2.6 meters) wide, and 13 feet (nearly 4 meters) tall. It provides 320 square feet (29.7 square meters) of interior space, plus two loft spaces, and although the footprint is relatively small, the layout makes great use of every available inch, creating a home that lacks for nothing.
They chose this model because it has a proper downstairs bedroom, two lofts, a spacious kitchen, a full bathroom, and storage galore, offering almost the same comfort and functionality as a conventional home. The kitchen is one of the first areas that catches the eye. Beautifully designed with blue-gray lower cabinets, white upper units, white stone countertops, and a tiled backsplash, the kitchen is a statement piece as you walk into the house.
Steph and Katie wanted the functionality of a conventional kitchen, so they equipped it with a full range, a microwave and vent hood combination, a vintage-style refrigerator, and even a dishwasher. They also have tons of storage, with deep drawers, upper cabinets, slide-out pantries, additional storage above the washer/dryer unit, and even kick-toe drawers for extra space.
Photo: Tiny House Expedition/YouTube screenshot There is no separation between the kitchen and the living room, and the design ensures easy passage and visual harmony between spaces. Furnished with a large mustard-yellow sofa, a couple of ottomans, and a TV on the wall, the lounge offers a comfortable place to unwind. The sofa also has built-in storage and is strategically placed between large windows to allow the occupants to feel immersed in their stunning surroundings.
Unlike the standard Modern Bohemian, which comes with a breakfast bar, the couple opted for a dinette designed for two. It features face-to-face benches and a table that can double as extra meal prep surface. Underneath the seating, there is more storage space, while a large window offers another lovely view of the property.
Photo: Tiny House Expedition/YouTube screenshot One of the main reasons Steph and Katie chose this model was its downstairs bedroom, which offers the comfort of a conventional room. It includes a full queen-size bed with adjacent nightstands and enough room to walk around both sides. It’s a storage bed that adds a lot of storage space that comes in handy for seasonal clothes and other items. The room also includes two wardrobes with both hanging space and drawers for clothing.
Having a master bedroom on the ground floor also means they don't have to climb a ladder to get to bed every night, and it leaves the two lofts available for other purposes. They turned one of the lofts into a cozy den. With a plush mattress, a skylight overhead, and additional windows, it feels almost like a treehouse.
This loft, located above the living room, is accessed via a staircase that is positioned at the end of the house and also incorporates several storage compartments, including a tall cabinet that stores larger items like a vacuum cleaner and mop. The second loft, accessed via a sliding ladder that stays out of the way when not in use, is primarily used for storage, although it could accommodate a double mattress as well.
Photo: Tiny House Expedition/YouTube screenshot Steph and Katie also have a full bathroom with a walk-through design. It includes a full-size stand-up shower with a tiled surround and glass enclosure, a flush toilet, and a vanity. The room was also customized with additional storage, including a cabinet above the toilet, shelves, and wall niches inside the shower.
Storage seems to be one of the most impressive aspects of this custom home . From the kitchen cabinetry and built-in compartments wherever possible to the storage bed, wardrobes, and separate loft, this house offers a space for everthing. This means the couple doesn't necessarily have to adopt a minimalist lifestyle just because they live in a tiny home.
The luxurious approach is evident throughout the house, but it also extends to what hides behind the walls. The tiny house has in-floor heating, an on-demand water heater, two air-conditioning units, and two air-exchange units, features that make it suitable for full-time living in any season.
Photo: Tiny House Expedition/YouTube screenshot Steph and Katie say the tiny house was a significant investment for them, but it was all worth it. It cost CAD $286,000, including delivery, setup, and skirting, and the office pod added another CAD $50,000.
They’ve been living in their island tiny home for one year already and say it was the best decision they’ve ever made. Their property has water access, but it’s in a remote location and has sloping terrain, which made building a conventional house a less practical option. A tiny house on wheels made more sense, allowing them to settle into this peaceful, mirific space in the middle of nature without giving up modern comforts.

Commissioner for Defence and Space Andrius Kubillius speaks at the Warsaw Security Forum. (Photo by Bartosz Głowacki)
WARSAW — The European Commission will continue to strengthen its defense capabilities to help defend Ukraine in its ongoing conflict with Russia, according to Commissioner for Defence and Space Andrius Kubillius.
“It’s very crucial to help Ukraine to defend itself and to defend the whole Europe,” Kubilius said here at the Warsaw Security Forum on Tuesday.
Kubillius’ comments come after the Trump administration has repeatedly called for Europe to become more self-reliant. However, Kubillius said his remarks are unrelated to US President Donald Trump’s statements alone, but rather a shift in global defense posturing as a whole.
“And that’s why [the] Commission president proposed to look into possibility to have what is called now the European Security Council, with member states, and … [the] United Kingdom, Ukraine, Norway, and Canada, which is close to Europe,” Kubilius said.
During her annual State of the Union Address in September, European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen pushed for the creation of the European Security Council , as Breaking Defense previously reported.
“For a long time we have discussed a leaders’ format focused on the security of our continent,” von der Leyen said at the time. “This is even more urgent now.”
The European Security Council could address the hurdle of fragmentation across the continent, Kibillius explained Tuesday.
Norwegian Minister of Defense Tore O. Sandvik agreed at the Warsaw Security Forum that Europe as a whole needs to band together.
“We have to take our responsibility. We are going to do that in Norway and we will go on for Europe,” he said.
“We now have a coalition of 11 countries in Europe supporting the anti-ballistic coalition, trying to develop anti-ballistic missile systems for Europe, because we need that,” Sandvik said.
“To a global level, we can support both countries in the Middle East, the US themselves, Europe, and our Pacific friends. What we can do in Ukraine, we can pass, we can develop, we can learn, and we can build new systems,” he added.
Hungarian Minister of Defence Romulusz Ruszin-Szendi said that under a new government, Budapest is aiming to focus more on the EU, particularly by getting the general public’s support.
“And we have a pretty large support. We have to do that. We have to change the mindset of the Hungarian society,” he said. “So, if you see what is happening in Hungary right now, more and more people are coming to the EU, more society is supporting them, and we try to introduce the Hungarian military to the society who can trust.”
Ruszin-Szendi also appealed for EU countries to have a better plan for potential future conflict, saying “if you see the different countries, the different interests, and different countries in Europe, see the threats, and the danger of aggression in Europe … [then] we have to find a way and we have to be able to deal with that.”
Netherlands Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Defence Dilan Yeşilgöz-Zegerius explained that showing a united front is especially important in a hybrid war — a war that uses propaganda and disinformation in addition to physical attacks.
This sentiment was also laid out in France’s 2035 national security plan released in September.
The next conflict, according to Yeşilgöz-Zegerius, will not be ended “with tanks and guns,” but rather will “start and end with communication and … who controls the narrative.”
“And I think that we have to be very aware of that. And we, in our part of Europe, need to turn up to get that narrative right,” she continued. “I think that our narrative needs to get stronger because the story of the other [side] is way less factual.

US EV Sales Sit at 6% While Europe Hits Record 23%
14 photos
Photo: Tesla
Electric vehicles currently enjoy a simply ridiculous 23.2 percent of the new car market in Europe. As per Motor Intelligence data, the US of A trails behind at 6 percent even though many of the subject electric vehicles feature similar tech specs and optional extras between the American and European markets.
September 30, 2025, can be considered a turning point for US-market electric vehicles, namely the day when the feds killed both the $7,500 incentive for new cars and the $4,000 incentive for used ones. Everyone spent that summer sprinting to the finish line, a frenzy that saw EVs hit 8.5 percent of sales that month.
By comparison, EVs made up 17.7 percent of the market in September 2025. A sizable gap, for sure, and the reasons for it go beyond the loss of incentives. Reuters correctly pointed out that European customers have more options than American buyers, including B-segment models aimed at ordinary budgets. More than 150 electric models were on sale in Europe in the first half of 2026, up from around 100 two years prior.
Considering that budget-friendly options can be purchased for less than €25,000 as of this writing, it's pretty simple to understand that affordability is of the essence on the Old Continent. Chinese brands have added more competition to the European market, bringing even cheaper alternatives that hinder legacy automakers like Volkswagen.
There's also the matter of countries that offer tax breaks. Considerably higher fuel prices than in the United States have supplied another nudge, making the prospect of ditching internal combustion more appealing. The American market, on the other hand, cannot make a similar pitch.
Photo: Tesla Worse still for electric vehicles in the United States market, the Trump administration has rolled back federal fuel economy and greenhouse gas regulations, reducing the regulatory pressure behind the EV push of many automakers. Tariffs and restrictions on Chinese-built vehicles, together with their software, have also made it harder for Chinese newcomers to enter the US of A.
For the time being, the perfect storm created by what is happening outside the United States and within it enabled hybrids to pick up the slack. US hybrid sales rose a whopping 23 percent through the first three quarters of 2026, accounting for 15.6 percent of the overall market. Looking at the bigger picture, they offer a better compromise for many prospective customers.
Promising better fuel economy than a conventional gas car without the need to plan around charging stops is the secret here. Used electric vehicles are finding buyers as well, with sales of used electric vehicles climbing 19 percent through September 2026. Reuters also notes that depreciation can make EVs particularly attractive, though battery health is a big problem for second-hand models.
Automakers are seeing different results, with Tesla US sales falling 14 percent in the first three quarters as opposed to an improvement of 29 percent for Rivian. Traditional brands have it rough, with Ford and General Motors recording 68 and 43 percent nosedives in the period from January 2026 through September 2026.
Simply put, the used market offers the best clue that America's appetite for electric vehicles is still there. With used sales up 19 percent, it becomes clear that American drivers are willing to go electric as long as the price makes sense.

Aston Martin DBX Sells for New Toyota Sequoia Money in the States
14 photos
Photo: Cars&Bids
Unless you’ve been living under a rock these past few years, then you know that it’s not only Lamborghini and Ferrari that are battling it out in the exotic crossover class, as so is Aston Martin .
The British company’s answer to the Urus and the Purosangue is called the DBX, and it entered production at the St. Athan factory in South Wales, UK, in mid-2020. Marek Reichman is responsible for the design, and he also signed the One-77, the 2012 Vanquish, the Vulcan, DB10 Concept, and other models. The DBX is related to other Astons, including the Vantage, the DB11, DB12, and DBS Superleggera.
Now, despite its blue-blooded nature, the Aston Martin DBX does not cost an arm and a leg in today’s used car market, especially if you are willing to settle for an earlier model year. That’s because the 2021 examples tend to venture into the $60,000 zone every now and then, though they can also exceed $80,000 quite easily. The later model years fetch a lot more than that, and a 2026MY can cost upward of $300,000 in today’s used car market Stateside.
As it happens ,the one pictured above is a 2021 model year, hence why it is on the affordable side of its class. It sports a Ceramic Blue paint finish on the outside, has an Obsidian Black cockpit, a clean New Jersey title, has never been involved in an accident, and is still located in Brooklyn, though it will relocate shortly, as it just found a new home for itself as part of an online auction that recently ended.
Photo: Cars&Bids More on that in a few moments, as first, we have to tell you that this Aston Martin DBX is a 1913 Edition. It features quite a few gizmos, including the adaptive air suspension, the 22-inch wheels, and the DB Elegance Pack. Besides these, the British exotic crossover in question sports leather upholstery, a panoramic glass roof, heated and ventilated seats at the front, twill carbon veneer, metal / composite extended trim inlay, smartphone connectivity, a 360-degree camera system, and other stuff.
The only modifications that the seller noted include the front and rear dashcams. Well, these and the tinted windows. As for the known flaws, these are the creases on the driver’s seat, some curb rash on the wheels, and the usual chips and scratches on the outside, some of which are touched-up. As previously mentioned, the Carfax history report shows now accidents in this vehicle’s past, and there are no mileage discrepancies either.
At the time of cataloging, this Aston Martin DBX had 38,900 miles (62,600 km) on the odo. It had its four tires replaced, the spark plugs replaced, and the engine oil and filter changed in July 2025, when the clock read 24,021 miles (38,658 km). The muffler was replaced in June 2025, an alignment was performed, and the engine oil and filter were changed in February 2024, at 15,900 miles (25,589 km), and the engine oil and filter were also changed in January 2023, at 9,633 miles (15,503 km).
Photo: Cars&Bids But what powers the British exotic crossover? Well, you likely know that it is a Mercedes-AMG-sourced mill. The twin-turbocharged V8 engine has a 4.0-liter displacement, and in this case, it developed 542 bhp (560 ps/405 kW) and 516 lb-ft (700 Nm) of torque when this DBX was new. Everything is channeled to the all-wheel drive system through a nine-speed automatic transmission. This model will run out of breath at 181 mph (292 kW), and will hit 62 mph (100 kph) in four and a half seconds.
A copy of the window sticker accompanies this Aston Martin DBX , joined by two keys, though one of them is missing the trim cover. These are the only things included in the sale. The seller is said to have represented the titled owner, who reportedly bought this high-riding Aston Martin in August 2025. The owner parted ways with this DBX because “ I just got a G 63 and have too many other cars, ” though they admitted that this one “ is a sweet ride, and pretty uncommon. ”
Now that you know plenty of things about this 2021 Aston Martin DBX, it is now time to reveal the selling price. So, how much do you think this exotic crossover fetched? When the gavel hit the table on October 13, 2026, at the Cars&Bids online auction , the highest bid was $72,500, and that number ended up being the selling sum. As mentioned in the title, that is pretty much new Toyota Sequoia money, as the latter starts at $65,725 for the 2026 model year, excluding destination, options, and dealer fees.
Sure, the Sequoia is something different indeed, not to mention that it’s a lot more reliable, and comes with the factory warranty, whereas the DBX is high maintenance. But if you had to choose between the two, which one would you get?

By Charlotte Goldstone
14 October 2026
Cyber extortion group ‘n0n’ has named 38 organisations across the global shipping and ports sector on its dark-web leak site, raising concerns that data may have been stolen.
Cybersecurity firm SOCRadar reported yesterday n0n published the listings in a single batch on 12 October. They included container terminals, shipping lines, port IT providers, and logistics businesses across 18 countries.
None of the maritime organisations named had publicly confirmed a breach at the time of writing.
South Korea accounted for 12 listings, including Busan terminal operators BNCT and Pusan Newport Co. The list included Brazilian port operators Santos Brasil, Portonave, and Superterminais; Singapore-based carrier ONE; China’s CULines; Taiwan’s TS Lines; Spain’s TTI Algeciras; and Morocco’s Eurogate Tanger.
The batch more than doubled n0n’s previously recorded victim count. The group emerged last month, listing 21 organisations across sectors including telecoms, retail, pharmaceuticals, and education.
SOCRadar said the pattern of data described in the listings suggested a possible common point of entry, rather than 38 separate network intrusions. According to the researchers, the relatively small, narrowly focused datasets and recurring document types could indicate information had been taken from an application or integration platform used by multiple organisations.
Reviewed samples included electronic data interchange (EDI) messages, container manifests, vessel schedules, gate movements, and terminal system configuration records. The claimed volumes ranged from 60mb for South Korean logistics company EUSU, to 2.4gb for Indonesia’s ILCS Pelindo.
The absence of matching infostealer credential records for many of the listed companies also complicates the theory that each intrusion began with stolen employee credentials, which SOCRadar identifies as a typical n0n access method.
But it warned that a shared system could extend the potential exposure beyond the organisations named on the leak site. EDI records and manifests can contain information on cargo movements, bookings, and commercial relationships involving shipping lines and other supply chain partners.
The pattern is reminiscent of mass-exploitation campaigns involving file-transfer software vulnerabilities, including the MOVEit Transfer attacks in 2023 and Cleo in 2024. However, SOCRadar said there was no evidence linking n0n to those incidents.
The cybercrime group has set a publication deadline of 19 October at 1.27pm UTC for the maritime listings reviewed by SOCRadar. Its leak site uses countdowns and status labels to pressure victims into paying.
Settlement demands have ranged from $2.4m to $14m, payable in bitcoin. The amounts did not appear to correspond with the volume of data allegedly stolen: EUSU Logistics faced a $14m demand for 60mb, with ILCS Pelindo at $2.4m for 2.4gb.
Some listings also offered victims the option of opening negotiations after paying 10% of the demand.
SOCRadar described n0n as a “financially motivated data-theft extortion operation” that generally avoids traditional ransomware deployment, instead threatening to publish stolen information. Its profile nevertheless includes techniques associated with encryption and interference with recovery, meaning disruptive activity cannot be ruled out.
The group’s claims remain unverified. Of its 21 earlier victims, SOCRadar said 19 remained at the claimed stage, one was listed as negotiating, and one, Chibitek, had experienced a data leak. Therefore, the 19 October deadline could provide the first substantive indication of what information n0n holds, and whether the alleged exposure extends across shared platforms.
SOCRadar warned that maritime businesses that exchange EDI with companies named in the attack should plan for the possibility that their operational data could appear in the 19 October release.
It advised them to identify the port community systems, EDI hubs, and file-transfer services handling their data; to check with providers for potential breaches, patch exposed systems, and investigate unusual access or bulk downloads. It also recommended rotating integration credentials, checking for compromised employee and supplier credentials, enforcing multi-factor authentication on remote access, and removing internet-exposed RDP services.
It also advised firms to prepare communications for customers and regulators in case data is exposed through a third party, and monitor n0n’s activity for further leak-site postings.

source_document.body:
Less-than-truckload rates hit a new high in the third quarter and are expected to finish the year even higher, according to a report from AFS Logistics and financial services firm TD Cowen.
The LTL rate-per-pound component of the TD Cowen-AFS Freight Index finished the third quarter 78.8% above its January 2018 baseline. That was 11.9 percentage points higher year over year and 1.1 points above the second quarter. The dataset is expected to end the fourth quarter 82.5% above the 2018 benchmark, which would be 14.7 points higher y/y.
High diesel fuel prices and extant “carrier pricing power” are driving the increases. The 80%-plus rate jump over an eight-year period also highlights the severity of cost inflation across carrier P&Ls (wages, health insurance, liability insurance, maintenance, etc.).
The dataset’s fuel surcharges were 79% higher y/y in September. Actual retail diesel prices were up y/y by 31% in July, 46% in August and 68% in September. (Less-than-truckload fuel surcharge mechanisms include a step function as diesel prices rise, resulting in margin accretion.)
Large public carriers have been able to capture mid-single-digit contractual rate increases through the downturn. Many are also pulling forward general rate increases given favorable sector fundamentals. Rate hikes on noncontractual LTL business used to occur annually. The cadence had been shortened to 11 months in recent years. Saia ( NASDAQ: SAIA ) installed a 7.1% GRI on July 6, which was 120 basis points higher and three months earlier than its 2025 increase.
The report showed LTL cost per shipment declined 2.8% sequentially (5.3% higher y/y) in the third quarter, as weight per shipment fell 3.4% (down 2.3% y/y), implying rate per pound was 0.6% higher (7.6% higher y/y).
Linehaul rates were 1.2% higher sequentially in the quarter even though length of haul declined 2.2%.
SONAR: LTL Monthly Cost per Hundredweight (LTL.USA) for 2026 (blue shaded area), 2025 (yellow line), 2024 (green line) and 2023 (pink line). The index shows the weighted average cost per hundredweight for LTL shipments (pallets only). To learn more about SONAR, click here .
Public carrier data has diverged from the index somewhat in recent months.
Tonnage among publicly traded LTL companies inflected positively y/y in March, with growth rates continuing to accelerate since. Mid-quarter updates from the group also showed y/y increases in weight per shipment during July and August, with XPO ( NYSE: XPO ) being the lone outlier. XPO’s freight mix now includes more shipments from SMBs, which tend to be smaller but carry better margins.
The group has indicated that the improved shipment weights result from freight previously lost to the truckload market returning to LTL networks as TL rates rise. Also, manufacturing activity has remained in growth territory in every month this year. The Institute for Supply Management’s Manufacturing PMI registered a 54.5 reading in September, with the new orders dataset logging a 55.3 reading. (A reading above 50 signals expansion, while one below 50 indicates contraction.)
Supply-side correction fueling TL rate surge
The TL rate-per-mile component of the index was 19.7% above the January 2018 baseline in the third quarter, 13.7 points higher y/y and 3.3 points above the second quarter, “as continued regulatory action, carrier exits and fuel shocks squeeze available capacity.”
The index is expected to increase to 23.4% above the benchmark during the fourth quarter, which would be 15.8 points higher y/y and the highest level registered since the 2022 first quarter.
The third-quarter earnings season begins Thursday when J.B. Hunt Transport Services ( NASDAQ: JBHT ) reports results after the market closes.
AFS Logistics is a non-asset-based 3PL providing audit and cost management services, managed transportation, and freight brokerage. It manages over $11 billion in transportation spend.
Why it matters? The TD Cowen-AFS Freight Index provides a rare look at past and future LTL rates. The dataset confirms key industry trends, including LTL rates hitting new highs in the third quarter and expected increases in the fourth quarter, driven by high fuel prices and carrier pricing power.

2027 Ineos Grenadier Helmsman Launches New Special Edition Series Inspired by 'The Elements'
6 photos
Photo: Ineos Automotive
The Ineos Grenadier off-road vehicle is preparing to enter the 2027 model year with a new special edition dubbed Helmsman in tow. More will come in the near future, all inspired by “the elements.”
Ineos Automotive Ltd is a British manufacturer of off-road vehicles based in London, established in 2016 after Sir Jim Ratcliffe, the chairman of the multinational chemicals company Ineos, failed to purchase the rights to build the classic Defender from Land Rover.
His version is a similar vehicle, named after the guy’s favorite pub, The Grenadier, in Belgravia, London, and has been produced since 2022 in Hambach, France, with a steel ladder chassis, beam axles, boxy styling, and BMW powertrains, including the B57 turbo diesel and B58 turbo inline-six plus the classic ZF eight-speed automatic transmission.
Over the years, the Ineos Grenadier has risen in popularity, and the company can easily name it a successful first-time project. More so, Ineos has been expanding the reach of the Grenadier in recent months with defense bids – they went into competition for the British Ministry of Defence’s Light Mobility Vehicle program back in September and also announced that the Italian Army and the Austrian government awarded them substantial orders and contracts for their enhanced protection versions of the Grenadier.
Of course, Ineos doesn’t forget that retail clients are very important, and inspired by one of the most important elements in nature, the tides, has introduced the Grenadier Helmsman model for the 2027 model year as the launch version of a new series of special editions. It “charts the course for a new line of special editions inspired by the elements Grenadier was designed to tackle” and will be available in both Station Wagon and Quartermaster versions.
Obviously aimed at fans with a passion for navigation, the Helmsman “reflects a nautical lifestyle and builds on the appeal of the standard Grenadier.” The new limited series has popular design elements taken from previous special editions and mixes them with a deep blue paint originally developed by Arcane Works.
The new 2027 Ineos Grenadier Helmsman also has exclusive badges, a Dark Exterior Pack featuring a black grille, dark skid plates, and all-new matte black roof rails, plus 17-inch diamond-cut alloy wheels. It also adds privacy glass, heated leather seats, carpet floor mats mixed with heavy-duty wash-down rubber flooring, locking wheel nuts, and the rear access ladder or load bay tub.
There are also features from the Smooth Pack like ambient lighting, front parking sensors, and auxiliary electrical points. In addition to the blue, there is also a Whiteout Blue metallic exterior paint option, also previously exclusive to Arcane Works models. The standard paints are Eldoret Blue and Scottish White, with optional contrast roofs in Inky Black or Scottish White. Inside, Helmsman introduces oyster-colored inserts for the black leather seats.
Pricing kicks off at £70,995 for the new 2027 Ineos Grenadier Helmsman, which is about $94k at the current exchange rate, but you need to hurry because it “will have a limited production window ahead of the next elements-inspired special edition.”
Built to work hard and play even harder, the Grenadier is in its element when recovering a boat or transporting kayaks to the coast. With this in mind, we have combined popular design features from previous limited editions with new oceanic hues to deliver the ideal 4X4 for watersports enthusiasts and seafarers. After three quarters of double-digit growth, it’s clear that our model line-up evolution is focused on bringing new customers to the brand who share our spirit of adventure,” explains Sagree Sardien, Global Sales Director at Ineos Grenadier.

Jordanian Armed Forces service members and U.S. Army service members select a target while aiming their Dronebuster during Eager Lion 2024 in Jordan, May 13, 2024. (U.S. Army photo by Sgt. Ivan Botts)
The Pentagon is working to grow an American drone industrial base capable of producing hundreds of thousands of systems next year. Great! But what happens if we succeed?
While drones are much like munitions in the numbers the US military will need to expend, we shouldn’t stockpile drones in warehouses. Technology, threats and tactics are changing too quickly. Large inventories of today’s best drones could become tomorrow’s stockpile of obsolescence .
Instead, we need to use them. And I don’t mean just for training. I mean, really use them, run them quite literally into the ground, and then see what we can learn.
The Defense Innovation Unit’s Deputy Director, Travis Metz, told the Senate Armed Services Committee this year that military training should consume drones in “the hundreds of thousands per year.” That’s an enormous number, and it creates an enormous opportunity. We need to use the elevated demand for those drones to train the industrial base to be able to support a war that quickly expends and iterates those platforms.
The industrial base can’t just be seen as a supplier to the military. As the rate of technological change accelerates, manufacturing capacity and its ability to quickly adapt will become an increasingly integral part of the force generation system. That means industry needs to be part of the exercise.
And scale matters. We won’t know if the industrial base can adapt at scale by ordering five prototypes — we need to know whether a system can be redesigned, built, trusted, delivered and employed in operationally useful quantities. You can’t do that without producing at mass.
The good news is, we’re already on the path. I attended both of the first two Drone Dominance Gauntlets, and the improvement between them was impressive. First, the drones were better and more reliable. The operators were better too. The Marines I watched had developed checklists and common language that helped them move quickly through setup and into flight. The test team was also better. Requirements were more clearly defined, scenarios were better differentiated and data collection and scoring were substantially more sophisticated.
But most impressively, the relationship between the vendors and operators had also changed. At times they looked less like customer and supplier and more like a single tactical-technical team. The operators knew what they wanted to do while vendors were able to show them how to make the technology accomplish that. From Gauntlet 1 to Gauntlet 2, the whole drone ecosystem adapted and improved. The important lesson: By consuming drones at significant scale, we simultaneously train the force, determine the next iteration of design and create the demand to build that next iteration.
So, what comes after the four Gauntlets conclude? Hopefully, we get more Gauntlets for different classes of systems. But we better not stop there. We should also take the most important lesson and institutionalize it.
If we think the only important training is the training done by warriors on the battlefield, we are losing sight of a very important facet of modern warfare. We need to exercise the industrial base as well.
Of course, consuming drones at this scale will not be cheap. But before you accuse me of wanting to set suitcases filled with $1,000 bills on fire, we need to recognize that drones stored in a warehouse can depreciate in combat value as technology, threats and tactics change. I’m not suggesting we purchase an extra 100,000 drones just to blow them up in tests; we need to plan to crash and replace some portion of the large quantities we’re already buying.
A drone deliberately consumed in a well-designed exercise can produce a different kind of combat value from the one stored in the warehouse. We have always recognized that spent munitions and jet fuel produce higher operator proficiency, test data, better tactics and exercised logistics. But by intelligently consuming drones, we will also benefit from industrial learning and improvements to the next generation of systems. Our objective isn’t to crash as many drones as possible, nor should it be to save every one of them for war. We need to find the balance between inventory and deliberate consumption that produces the most combat value for the money.
We already have many of the pieces. The Drone Dominance Program is testing both drone performance and manufacturing readiness. Project Flytrap puts emerging technology into soldiers’ hands in operationally representative environments, and it’s already connected through a series of exercises. Major exercises provide increasingly realistic operational problems, and the Department of War is experimenting with ways to assess manufacturing readiness. Now we need to connect them and integrate manufacturing between them. Together, they could become a continuous industrial exercise that teaches how to adapt when we find ourselves in the next major conflict.
Imagine a major exercise in which thousands of drones are treated as fully consumable. Both sides have drones and counter-drone systems. Operators employ their systems while testers collect data. Engineers, supply-chain experts, acquisition professionals and manufacturers are connected to what is happening in the field.
Once one side finds a significant advantage, that may be the end of that operational event, but that would then trigger the next phase of the industrial exercise. We start the clock. Operators and testers determine what went right and what went wrong. Maybe they had an advantage in tactics but a disadvantage with the software interface. Maybe an adversary found a vulnerability in a communications link. Maybe a sensor, payload, antenna, component, or airframe needs to change.
Industry takes these lessons and immediately starts working.
Can it redesign the system? Can suppliers support the change? Can the government establish enough trust in the modified system to use it? Can the factory reconfigure? Can it produce the new version in quantities that matter? Can logistics get it back to the unit? Can operators learn the changes?
Some parts of the system will likely adapt faster than others. Finding this disparity is exactly what we need. The exercise will expose the bottlenecks that need to be fixed.
Then train again. And again. And again. Faster and faster. This could be done through a string of already existing exercises, modified to collect the right data and insert vendors at the tactical level. One exercise could discover a vulnerability, industry could adapt between events, and the next exercise could test the answer.
In effect, the industrial exercise never really ends. Individual exercises and events become iterations in a continuously adapting campaign to see what failed, what changed, at what scale, how long each step took and where we need to intervene.
Expending drones on this scale will create problems of their own. We’ll have to figure out how to recover systems, harvest useful components, handle damaged batteries, recycle materials and dispose of what cannot reasonably be recovered. Good. Those are wartime logistics problems and it’s time to start learning those lessons too.
We can’t simply replicate what Ukraine did in their drone war. The United States would likely face different constraints and would integrate drones into Joint All-Domain Operations. What we should borrow is Ukraine’s rate of learning and adapting drones to fit their operational needs.
We train pilots by flying, infantry by shooting and staffs through exercises because we don’t want to discover during wartime whether they can perform their missions. If manufacturing and adaptation are increasingly becoming part of aggregate combat power, that same logic should apply to our industrial base.
The objective shouldn’t be to enter the next war with the world’s largest warehouse of drones. It should be to enter it with the world’s most practiced system for designing, building and delivering drones. And it might take a whole lot more than crashing 100,000 drones to get there.
Col. Dustin Thomas is the Commander of DCMA’s Unmanned Systems – Experimental Command (US-X). US-X provides contract oversight for unmanned systems of all sizes across all domains and manages the Blue List. Col. Thomas previously led Black Phoenix, an innovation team focused on designing, building and flying small unmanned systems in less than 24 hours, and founded Game of Drones, an experimentation event focused on the rapid integration of new technology into unmanned systems.

VIENNA — Estonia’s new defense minister said his country should consider buying light jet aircraft to shoot down Russia’s faster, jet-powered attack drones.
Martin Herem, a retired general who took office Sept. 16, floated the idea in interviews after meeting Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy in Kyiv. He told The Baltic Sentinel and the daily Postimees that Estonia should study the option, saying air-to-air weapons are the most effective counter to the drones.
He gave no aircraft type, budget or timeline.
Herem has not committed to buying anything. He told The Baltic Sentinel he is also looking at computer-controlled cannons, heavy machine guns and fast, jet-powered interceptor drones. He noted that Estonia already has pilots, air-control expertise and L-39 trainers.
The two L-39 Albatros trainers Estonia uses are leased, according to the Estonian military’s website . Their civilian status and lease terms would complicate any move to arm them, the former head of Estonia’s air force said back in April .
The proposal responds to a threat that is growing fast. Yuriy Ihnat, a Ukrainian air force spokesman, said Ukraine intercepted about 40% of jet-powered drones in July and 60% in August, according to Hromadske . In the same period, the number of jet-powered drones fired at Ukraine increased from a few hundred to several thousands a month. Ukraine’s defense ministry puts their speed at more than 400 kilometers per hour.
None of the three Baltic states have their own fighter fleet. NATO allies police their skies on rotation, and allied jets have shot down drones over Latvia in June and over Lithuania on Sept. 15. Estonia’s air-policing rotation currently includes Turkish F-16s at Ämari. Spanish F-18s were scheduled to depart after their rotation in “early October,” according to the Estonian military .
Neither Latvia nor Lithuania have floated buying jet aircraft of their own. Both are putting money into cheaper counter-drone layers instead, and Latvia is considering the Embraer’s A-29 Super Tucano, a light turboprop fighter aircraft, for air-defense missions.
Lithuania’s government on Sept. 2 authorized the defense ministry to skip standard procurement rules to buy trial batches of interceptor drones and radars. Defense Minister Robertas Kaunas said Vilnius would favor systems already tested in Ukraine. Lithuania is also testing Ukraine’s SkyFortress acoustic detection system.
Latvia is building what State Secretary Airis Rikveilis called a “wall of drones” on its eastern border. It will combine radars, interceptor drones and command equipment.
NATO planners have repeatedly said that using heavy fighters against small drones is disproportionately expensive. Interceptor drones and ground-based air defenses often cost substantially less to procure and to operate.

By Alexander Whiteman
14 October 2026
Gemini may be relaunching connections between the Far East and Middle East this weekend, to restore direct ocean links, but after replacing Jebel Ali calls, Khor Fakkan appears to be showing signs of buckling under the pressure.
As reported by The Loadstar yesterday, the relaunched service, marketed as AGX by Hapag-Lloyd and FM1 by Maersk, is set to operate under a revised rotation that sees Khor Fakkan replace Jebel Ali, because of the US-Iran war, but warning signs of congestion have appeared at the Emirati gateway.
A Kuehne+Nagel update that Khor Fakkan and Fujairah “taking on a lot of the volumes shifted to ports outside the Strait of Hormuz in recent months” had led to congestion across the UAE’s corridors, with the two ports now the “main pressure points in the region”.
It added: “Through Fujairah and Khor Fakkan, transit times vary by destination, while final-mile delivery and corridor connectivity remain under the control of UAE government-affiliated logistics providers.
“However, as congestion in Jeddah decreases, we expect cargo flows to redistribute towards alternative gateways, including Jeddah, Aqaba, and Salalah. Looking ahead, we expect Khor Fakkan and Fujairah to remain under significant pressure in the coming weeks.”
This was also recognised by Maersk, which said in its latest operational update: “Vessel congestion and limited berth availability at Khor Fakkan, together with high yard utilisation, road congestion and extended truck waiting times, are delaying cargo clearance.”
Meanwhile, Expeditors has somewhat downplayed the extent of the problem, noting that “UAE gateways remain largely unaffected and outside the Strait risk area”, but nonetheless added that Khor Fakkan and Fujairah were “showing signs of congestion”.
With Gemini’s relaunched service scheduled for 17 October, on its Qingdao-Ningbo-Tanjung Pelepas-Khor Fakkan-Singapore-Qingdao rotation, the congestion issues have raised questions as to how beneficial the additional capacity will prove for shippers.
Maersk said that it would be relocating some boxes to an inland container depot at Sajja, which it hoped would help ease pressure on the port, while it is planning for the possible redirection of some shipments to Jebel Ali.
Even so, cargo arriving at ports still needs to reach its final destination, and hauliers and logistics operators have been crying out for support to provide additional hinterland connectivity, with trucking the most obvious solution.
However accessing that capacity has become a key hurdle, with forwarders telling The Loadstar that , since the outset of the war, this capacity was being “hoovered up” by “forwarders with the biggest pockets, rather than shipments with the most need”.

Tesla launched a "Lite" variant of FSD V14 for HW3 vehicles in June, but only on Model 3 and Model Y vehicles. The Model S and Model X were left behind, but that is now changing. Tesla confirmed that the FSD V14.3 Lite is rolling out to legacy Model S and Model X equipped with Intel processors. Vehicles that combine HW3 with MCU3 (Ryzen) will likely follow shortly.
Tesla FSD development hit a snag on HW3 vehicles when the ever-increasing hardware requirements could no longer be met by older hardware. Tesla promised to address the situation, but the process took more than two years. Until recently, Teslas equipped with HW3 Autopilot computers were stuck on FSD V12 because newer builds could not run on their outdated computers.
Things changed for the better in June, when Model 3 and Model Y equipped with HW3 processors got a "Lite" variant of the FSD V14. As Tesla explained at the time, this was a distilled variant of the FSD V14 software that runs on HW4 vehicles. This introduced some limitations , including a longer reaction time that could affect safety in unpredictable ways. However, it was a step up from the old V12 builds.
While Model 3 and Model Y owners were already finding the limits of the new FSD V14 Lite software, Model S and Model X owners could only dream. Hopes got a boost in September, when Tesla began to test FSD V14 Lite on Model S and Model X. However, the tests were limited to early access (Wave1) testers, and we've seen no further evidence that Tesla was advancing with FSD V14 Lite on Model S/X. Until now, that is.
The carmaker confirmed that FSD V14 Lite starts rolling out to Model S and Model X vehicles equipped with an Intel MCU. These are considered "legacy" vehicles, some built in 2017 or even earlier. That's because Tesla offered a MCU2 retrofit to MCU1 vehicles for a cool $2,500. Those who also paid FSD in full got a free HW2/HW2.5 to HW3 upgrade, thus making their vehicles eligible to run FSD V14.3 Lite in the latest software update.
The same update (2026.38.5.1) also includes the Halloween update, FSD V14.3.12, and the Automatic Collision Evasion feature. Still, they are irrelevant to legacy HW3 Model S/X vehicles. Halloween Update is currently supported on Ryzen processors only, while FSD V14.3.12 and ACE are HW4-exclusive.
So far, HW3-equipped Model S/X with Ryzen MCUs haven't gotten the latest FSD V14.3 Lite update, but that is likely to change shortly. Select AMD-based HW3 Model S/X vehicles have received previous FSD V14 Lite builds. However, the rollout has been very limited, probably because Tesla was still testing it.
Based on the experience of Model 3/Y owners who received FSD V14 Lite, the automated driving software puts a lot of strain on the HW3 computers. This can lead to overheating and the familiar "red hands" error. A thorough cleaning of the cooling radiators is advised before testing FSD on older vehicles. Since his release from prison in 2022, Martin Shkreli has traded stocks and publicly opined on news events, damaging reputations and sinking share prices for small biotechs including Capricor and Cassava, the FTC alleges.
Martin Shkreli, the scorned “pharma bro” who drew the ire of patients for his actions as a pharmaceutical company executive, has come under the scrutiny of the Federal Trade Commission for allegedly violating his lifetime ban from the industry.
The FTC asked a judge to hold Shkreli in contempt, presenting evidence that he has “flagrantly and repeatedly” violated the court order that has been in place since 2022, according to a Tuesday press release . The disgraced executive has been trading in pharma stocks and “broadcasting his opinions about the business and management of many pharmaceutical industry companies,” according to the complaint.
Indeed, Shkreli recently weighed in on the saga of Capricor Therapeutics , recommending that CEO Linda Marbán and a researcher receive prison time.
“Having been myself, I am loathe to recommend prison. In this case, I’m making sure you’re both going,” Shkreli wrote in a July 27 post on X captured by BioSpace . “Playing with patient data is a line you cannot cross. In my worst hour I’d never.”
A screengrab of an X post by former pharma executive Martin Shkreli.
BioSpace
‘Egregious, deliberate, repetitive’
In the complaint , the FTC recapped the actions that led to the lifetime ban. Shkreli was originally found guilty of securities fraud in 2018 and sentenced to seven years in prison. In a separate case brought by the FTC in 2020, a court in 2022 found that Shkreli, in his capacity as executive of companies Vyera Pharmaceuticals and Phoenixus , and his co-defendants executed an anticompetitive scheme to prevent the entry of low-cost generics to the market.
The defendants were found to have jacked up the price of Daraprim, a drug used to treat a potentially deadly parasitic infection called toxoplasmosis, from $17.50 to $750 per pill.
Shkreli was found guilty of organizing an illegal scheme to perpetuate a monopoly for the medication. He was banned from the pharma industry for life due to his “egregious, deliberate, repetitive, long-running and ultimately dangerous illegal conduct,” according to the complaint. Shkreli was also fined over $64 million.
The ban specifically stated that Shkreli was not to “directly or indirectly” participate in the industry. He was also not to own any stocks of relevant companies or take any direct or indirect action to influence or control the management or business of a pharma company.
Martin Shkreli testifying before the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform in 2016.
House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform , Wikimedia Commons
Nevertheless, since his early release in May 2022, Shkreli “has publicized his order violations” via posts on YouTube, X and Reddit, the FTC said.
“The motion alleges that, while livestreaming his trades in pharmaceutical industry stocks, Shkreli told his viewers ‘I’m showing you how to trade and invest in biotech,’” the FTC wrote.
Shkreli also showed viewers how to short a stock, which is when traders bet that a stock will decline rather than perform well, according to the FTC.
The complaint details his efforts to short Cassava Sciences’ stock in 2024. The company is developing the Alzheimer’s disease drug simufilam. Shkreli dedicated hours of livestreams to the company, declaring that “the odds that this drug works is, like . . . 1%,” according to the complaint.
“On November 24, 2024, he declared that if Cassava’s trial was successful, he would shave his head, delete his social media accounts, change his name to Martina, move to Haiti, and ‘retire from business completely,’” the FTC said.
In total, Shkreli has traded in dozens of pharma and biotech stocks, including Amgen, AstraZeneca, Novo, Intellia Therapeutics, Viking Therapeutics, Nuvation Bio, Neumora Therapeutics, Anavex Life Sciences and many more, according to the complaint.
The FTC also provided a much longer list of companies that Shkreli has spoken about or traded in during his livestreams, including Eli Lilly, Sarepta Therapeutics, Biogen and uniQure.
Moving the markets
Throughout the complaint, the FTC included screengrabs of Shkreli’s social media commentary. The activity continued into this year, when Shkreli issued a new “trading challenge” with an account that had a balance of $10 million. This round included trades in Pfizer, Moderna and others.
“Shkreli continues to dedicate much of his now-frequent livestreams to discussing pharmaceutical company stocks and their relative merits,” the FTC complaint said.
Shkreli ultimately lost a short he placed against Capricor, writing this year that he “lost millions” and, in a profane and misogynistic X post that was included in the FTC complaint, threatened to send Marbán to jail. Nevertheless, his public statements urging his followers to short the stock at one point sent the biotech’s shares down 17%, according to the FTC.
“Shkreli’s ability to move the market with his spoken and written assaults has real consequences for the small biotech companies that are the subject of his short attacks,” the FTC explained in the complaint. “With no products generating revenue, a clinical-stage biotech company relies entirely on investors to sustain them until they can get their product approved and on the market. When their stock price drops and their reputation is under attack, the company may be unable to raise the needed funds through the typical path of additional public stock offerings.”
Cassava, for instance, “facing such a cash crunch in the wake of Shkreli’s successful short attacks,” was forced to lay off staff , the agency said.
The FTC has asked the court to hold Shkreli in contempt, force him to divest his shares and issue a fine in the amount he has profited. Shkreli should also face escalating penalties for continued violations of the lifetime ban, the agency said.

Pilot Travel Centers and Tesla have opened their first Megacharger site for heavy-duty electric trucks, Pilot said Oct. 8 . The site, at a Pilot travel center in Ellabell, Ga., has six charging stalls.
Twelve more heavy-duty sites are under construction, and three are nearly finished: a Flying J in Tulare, Calif., scheduled to open Oct. 9; a Flying J in Fort Stockton, Texas; and a Pilot in North Las Vegas, Nev.
Each site will have four to eight stalls running Tesla’s V4 cabinet technology. According to Tesla, each stall can deliver up to 1.2 megawatts, enough for a Tesla Semi to recover 60% of its charge in 30 minutes.
Pilot, a Berkshire Hathaway subsidiary based in Knoxville, Tenn., operates more than 900 locations in 43 states and five Canadian provinces. The Megacharger network is planned for select locations along I-5, I-10, and other major freight corridors in California, Georgia, Indiana, Nevada, and Texas.
“Pilot is proud to bring heavy-duty charging directly to key trucking routes and pair it with the services and amenities drivers rely on,” said Shannon Sturgil, senior vice president of alternative fuels at Pilot.
Ellabell’s opening came later than Pilot projected. When the companies announced the partnership in January , Pilot said construction would begin in the first half of 2026 and the first sites would open in the summer.
The January announcement also named New Mexico among the initial states. The October release drops it and lists Indiana.
The chargers are arriving as Tesla moves the Semi into high-volume production , which started at its Sparks, Nev., factory on Sept. 24. Tesla expects more than 30 charging stations and over 200 megawatt-capable posts by year-end, including the Pilot sites. The plant is designed for 50,000 trucks a year.
Pilot said the heavy-duty sites build on its passenger EV charging network and its renewable diesel and biodiesel offerings.
“With these initial locations, we’re making fleet electrification a more accessible option for long-haul transportation,” Sturgil said.

Verdiva Bio has pulled the plug on a Phase 2 study testing its lead GLP-1 drug candidate as an oral maintenance option for patients with overweight and obesity but will continue developing the medicine for other weight loss indications.
The discontinuation was a “business decision” and not based on safety findings, according to a federal clinical trials database . The study was testing VRB-101 (oral ecnoglutide) in patients who had undergone at least six months of subcutaneous treatment with Novo’s semaglutide or Eli Lilly’s tirzepatide and had achieved 10% weight loss or greater. Eight patients were enrolled at the time of the study’s cancellation.
“We have refined our clinical development plans for VRB-101 in light of market evolution,” a Verdiva spokesperson told BioSpace in an email on Wednesday, responding to questions about the biotech’s decision to discontinue the mid-stage trial.
Verdiva licensed VRB-101 from Chinese company Sciwind Biosciences, paying $70 million upfront and putting more than $2.4 billion on the line in milestone payments. The deal was signed in 2024 but was revealed in January 2025, alongside the announcement of Verdiva’s launch and closing of a $411 million series A round.
Aside from VRB-101, Verdiva also obtained from Sciwind two amylin analogs, one designed as a weekly oral treatment and the other a long-acting subcutaneous injection.
A subcutaneous version of ecnoglutide is approved for diabetes and chronic weight management in China, where Pfizer owns the drug’s commercialization rights through a February agreement with Sciwind. The pharma put up to $495 million on the line for ecnoglutide.
In June, data from a head-to-head Phase 2 trial in China showed that subcutaneous ecnoglutide elicited 35% greater weight loss than Novo’s semaglutide, which is approved for the indication in the U.S. as Wegovy. At 20 weeks, patients on ecnoglutide lost 12.8% of their body weight on average, versus 9.5% in semaglutide controls, with the difference reaching statistical significance, Sciwind said. The ongoing trial, called SLIMMER-UP-SWITCH , enrolled 163 adults with obesity who were randomly assigned to receive ecnoglutide or semaglutide. The study’s primary outcome is change in body weight.
Verdiva now hopes to bring the drug’s oral version to the market. Despite the discontinued mid-stage study, the biotech is actively advancing VBR-101—both as a monotherapy and in combination with the company’s two amylin assets. A separate Phase 2 study of VRB-101, dubbed EVOLVE-2, wrapped up in July, though the biotech has yet to release data .
“We continue to develop VRB-101 as a potential monotherapy, while ensuring the program generates the data needed to inform its potential role alongside our amylin portfolio,” the Verdiva spokesperson said. “Data from the EVOLVE-2 study is being assessed and we’ll provide an update on the clinical trial when we can.”
With its Sciwind-originated pipeline, Verdiva seeks to compete in the crowded obesity arena, currently dominated on both the injectable and oral fronts by Novo and Lilly.

South Korea’s President Lee Jae-myung says he remains committed to establishing container shipping services between Busan and Europe via the Northern Sea Route by 2030, despite lukewarm commercial interest.
He said ferry operator Panstar Line’s test voyage, with the 2,758 teu Panstar Acro , helped pave the way for the commercial viability of Arctic shipping.
The ship had arrived back in Busan on Sunday, after the 40-day round-trip to Felixstowe and Rotterdam.
Although cargo volumes were below target, just 837 teu loaded on Panstar Acro , Mr Lee hailed the voyage as a success.
He wrote on X : “The ship completed the journey to Europe in a mere 20 days via the Arctic, whereas the Suez Canal route would have taken almost a month. We will continue to prepare for an Arctic shipping era, and this test trip would create new opportunities for businesses.”
Rising global temperatures have melted more Arctic ice, making the Northern Sea Route (NSR) seem a feasible substitute for the Suez Canal, particularly given the Red Sea crisis and US/Israel-Iran tensions.
Promoting Arctic shipping also aligns with the government’s plan to build an economic zone in the south, anchored by Busan, the nation’s primary container port.
The Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries plans to analyse details of the voyage to determine how Arctic shipping could become more commercially viable.
Yet enthusiasm among South Korean shipowners remains muted. At an industry gathering, they noted that, once the Middle East crisis was resolved, the NSR could cease to be an appealing alternative to the Suez Canal route.
Shipping executives pointed out that the NSR could only be navigated between August and November, when the Arctic ice thaws enough to allow passage. Draught limitations also make it impossible to operate large containerships on the route, unlike through the canal.
Notably, Panstar was the sole bidder when the ministry sought operators for the test voyage in May – prohibitive costs, including insurance and modifications for polar navigation, deterred other companies.
In August, the Korea Maritime Institute released a study showing the cost per teu of operating containerships through the Arctic from Busan to Rotterdam was around 55% greater than going via Suez, cancelling the advantage of the shorter sailing time.
During the “welcome-back” ceremony for Panstar Acro yesterday, President Lee said he was aware of commercial scepticism towards the NSR.
He added: “There are people concerned about the costs, but when we gain more experience and attract more cargo on Arctic routes, we can reduce costs and increase trust in the service.”

KYIV, Ukraine — Russia is still using fast jet-powered drones to batter Ukraine’s energy facilities, bridges and other critical infrastructure at speeds beyond the reach of most of Kyiv’s drone interceptors, despite U.S. President Donald Trump’s unilateral announcement on Sunday of an energy ceasefire between the two countries.
Russia began using the jets heavily in July, when their numbers jumped fivefold from the previous month. They can now reach speeds of up to 373 mph (600 km/h) — more than three times the speed of the propeller-driven Geran-2 drones they evolved from — far exceeding the top velocity of the average Ukrainian interceptor drone, air force officials told lawmakers last week.
To stop the drones, Ukraine must instead rely on F-16s, newly installed machine gun turrets that use artificial intelligence to aim and costly air-defense missiles that are in short supply globally.
“Ukraine did not strike Russian oil refining and the energy sector in general for two days after the American president announced a ceasefire in the energy sector. But Russia did not listen to the American president,” Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy wrote after jets seriously damaged a gas production facility in the northeastern Kharkiv region on Sunday night.
Russia launched 167 missiles and drones overnight Tuesday into Wednesday, including 77 jet-powered drones, which officials said struck one of Kyiv’s main power plants and left 600,000 without power.
Ukraine’s Air Force says they are beginning to field more effective countermeasures, but with Russia continuing to optimize the design of jet-powered drones to destroy critical infrastructure, the development of jets and anti-jet interceptors has become the latest neck-and-neck technology race on the battlefield.
Iran shipped Russia its first Shahed-131 and Shahed-136 drones in mid-August 2022, and Moscow rebranded them the Geran-1 and Geran-2 and was firing them at Ukrainian civilian infrastructure by that October.
Those propeller-driven drones were slow enough for Ukraine to build an economical defense around mobile fire teams and cheap interceptor drones rather than spending scarce missiles on every Shahed, and in February the interceptors accounted for more than 70% of Shahed downings over Kyiv .
The jet-powered Gerans are outrunning that defense, and Russia has since stopped building the slower Geran-3 and ramped up production of the Geran-4, which cruises at 217 to 311 mph (350 to 500 km/h), and the missile-shaped Geran-5, which carries a 90-kilogram (198-pound) warhead, Militarnyi reported in August, citing Ukraine’s military intelligence agency, known as HUR.
“The Geran-5 flies 150km/h faster than the Geran-4, so the goal is to intercept from the front rather than the rear — a much harder problem to solve,” an engineer at a Ukrainian defense contractor told the Kyiv Independent .
And they are still getting faster, with the Air Force projecting speeds of 500 to 560 mph (800 to 900 km/h), though none have been recorded yet, its deputy commander, Col. Yurii Cherevashenko, told a parliamentary commission Oct. 6.
A Geran-4 version Russia began flying this autumn is built to take out infrastructure, navigating by a U.S.-made magnetometer and an optical system and carrying a new warhead designed to cut bridges and power line supports, HUR said in an Oct. 5 statement .
The new 88-pound (40-kilogram) warhead “was created specifically to destroy high-voltage pylons and iron bridge structures,” Serhii “Flash” Beskrestnov, an EW expert and adviser to Zelenskyy, wrote on Telegram Sept. 30 when Russia was first spotted using the upgrade on a jet drone.
These optimized Russian jet drones hit Kyiv’s South Bridge, which carries cars and metro trains across the Dnipro River, at least five times on Oct. 1 and 2, once exploding near a pier as a train crossed overhead, then struck the city’s North Bridge on Oct. 3, officials said.
Ukrainian interceptors stopped roughly 90% of the older propeller-driven drones , but against the jets, the interception rate has been significantly lower.
“Initially, we saw a very low interception rate in Ukraine. It then rose to more than 30%, and in recent nights it has increased to over 50%,” Matthias Lehna, vice president of German drone maker Quantum Systems, told Ukrinform last week.
Air force officials reported downing 77% of incoming jet-powered drones on Tuesday night.
Ukraine put its first jet interceptor, the Alexa Spatium, into service only on Aug. 21, and a handful of other prototypes, including Wild Hornets’ STING S and SkyFall’s P1-SUN Jetkiller, have successfully downed a small number of Geran-5s, according to officials speaking to the Kyiv Independent.
Fourteen companies are flight-testing jet interceptors with the Air Force, and three have shown promising results, but the deputy air force commander said officials don’t expect the jet interceptors to be delivered at the scale Ukraine needs until the end of November at the earliest.
Jet drones already make up approximately 40% of the drones Russia launches and the Air Force expects that share to reach up to 80% of total attacks.

A Nebraska traffic stop uncovered more than $250,000 in stolen copper inside a semi-truck on October 7. Lancaster County’s Criminal Interdiction Unit stopped the vehicle around 2 p.m. on Interstate 80. Deputies saw the trailer leaning heavily after the load shifted toward the passenger side. The driver could not provide vehicle registration, a bill of lading or basic freight details.
Authorities identified the driver as 22-year-old Raman Pal of Tracy, California. Pal could not explain what he hauled, where pickup occurred or the destination. Deputies received consent to search the truck and trailer. Inside, they found 11 pallets of copper wire weighing 43,937 pounds and two bolt cutters.
Copper load had passed Iowa destination
Deputies found a bill of lading during the vehicle search. It listed Imperial Metal Group in Chicago as the pickup location. Court records identify Imperial Metal Group as the owner of the stolen copper. Lakeside Auto Recyclers, a Carter Lake, Iowa, recycling company, was the listed destination.
Investigators stopped Pal near Lincoln after the truck had already passed Carter Lake. Lakeside Auto Recyclers confirmed the vehicle was off route while traveling westbound. The affidavit does not explain why Pal continued beyond the listed destination.
The affidavit states Get There Real Quick LLC should have delivered the shipment. FMCSA records list the Illinois carrier under USDOT 4381300 and MC 1717529. Get There Real Quick operates interstate with six power units and 10 drivers. Lakeside Auto Recyclers told deputies Nawab Xpress Inc. should not possess the load.
Pal’s truck displayed Nawab Xpress and USDOT 4172559. FMCSA records list the California company as an interstate carrier. Nawab Xpress operates with one power unit and one driver. The affidavit does not explain how Nawab Xpress obtained the shipment.
Investigators contacted Imperial Metal Group President Zach Spellman during the stop. Spellman confirmed the copper belonged to his company. He told deputies the shipment was stolen because the correct carrier did not possess it. The trailer also lacked the load lock and seal Imperial required.
Spellman told investigators this was Imperial Metal Group’s fourth stolen metal load this year. He said all four disappeared “in the same fashion.” The combined value exceeded $1 million, according to the sheriff’s briefing. Records do not establish whether the same people handled those losses.
Investigation could extend nationwide
Court records show prosecutors charged Pal with criminal impersonation and theft by unlawful taking over $5,000. The complaint identifies the stolen property as belonging to The Imperial Group LLC. Deputies also found two identification cards carrying different names inside the cab. One matched Pal’s actual California identification, according to the affidavit.
The affidavit does not identify a freight broker or explain how Pal obtained the shipment in Chicago. It also does not describe a fictitious pickup or name any federal agency involved. Deputies placed the truck and trailer on a criminal hold after Pal’s arrest. Investigators continue working to determine how the load changed hands.
FreightWaves contacted the Lancaster County Sheriff’s Office, Imperial Group and Lakeside Auto Recyclers for additional information. None had responded before publication. Investigators have not established whether the same people were involved in Imperial Metal Group’s four thefts. “There’s a lot more people involved in this than just the 22-year-old,” the sheriff’s office told reporters.
Why it matters
The case shows how a high-value load can leave the proper carrier’s control and keep moving without immediate detection. That gap can turn a single pickup failure into a six-figure cargo loss before anyone realizes the shipment is off course.
CFCO
In my opinion, Certified Fraud Compliance Officer training can help teams catch carrier, driver and document mismatches before releasing a load. A repeatable verification process creates another checkpoint before high-value freight leaves the shipper’s control.

Pennsylvania will spend more than $371 million at the of Philadelphia, a commitment that officials say will unlock $466 million in federal grants and private investment as part of a $837 million expansion described as the largest in the hub’s history.
The plan is expected to increase container capacity by 122% and automobile capacity by 18%, add more than 6,000 jobs, and generate $45 million in annual state and local tax revenue.
PhilaPort will use the state funding, together with two U.S. Department of Transportation grants, to build a new 2,000-foot berth at Southport Marine Terminal —the port’s first new berth in more than 50 years.
“PhilaPort has a long and storied history that spans back over 300 years to the very founding of our Commonwealth,” said Gov. Josh Shapiro, at a press conference Tuesday. “It was here where goods produced in Philadelphia embarked for destinations around the globe, and today, the port remains a major player in global trade and a critical piece of our economy. This is a game changer for PhilaPort and it builds on our work to grow the economy and create real opportunity for Pennsylvanians.”
As a specialized mid-Atlantic gateway , Philadelphia handled a record 889,268 TEUs in 2025, compared with 8.9 million TEUs at New York-New Jersey and 5.7 million TEUs at Savannah.
PhilaPort currently supports more than 8,000 jobs and contributed nearly $1.2 billion in economic output across Pennsylvania in 2025, according state data. The expansion is projected to lift port-related employment to about 14,000.
The program also includes dredging at Southport, land acquisition, infrastructure improvements, and new cranes and cargo-handling equipment. Project components include $31 million for Southport dredging, $145 million for reclamation work at Southport Berth II and the North Wharf, and $58.1 million for cranes and other equipment.
Private commitments include $100 million each from terminal operator Holt Logistics and vehicle-processing company Glovis America.
The expansion would transform the 152-acre Mustin Yard parcel adjacent to Southport for container and automobile cargo, while the new berth would add vessel capacity at Southport. Officials told local media that auto capacity gains would amount to more than 100,000 additional vehicles annually.
Construction is expected to begin once permitting and contracting are complete, with port officials projecting a ground-breaking in early 2027.
The announcement positions Philadelphia to compete for additional container and automobile business as East Coast ports seek to expand capacity. State officials said the investment is intended to strengthen PhilaPort’s role as a global trade hub and support future cargo growth.
